SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC AND MACT, AT RAICHUR, IN MVC.NO.652/2021 AND PLEASED TO ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION AND PLEASED FASTENED ENTIRE LIABILITY ON RESONDENT NO.2 CORPORATION, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE R.NATARAJ  AND  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TYAGARAJA N. INAVALLY  CAV JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TYAGARAJA N. INAVALLY)

Being aggrieved by the amount of compensation awarded by the learned II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Raichur,
(henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC.No.652/2021 vide judgment and award dated 21.02.2025 the claimant has come up with the present appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: NC: 2026:KHC-K:15-DB HC-KAR 2.

The facts of the case of the claimant in brief are that on 29.08.2021 at about 07.30. p.m. he was riding a motorcycle from Neermanvi and when he reached near Radhakrishna Camp Limits on Sirwar - Manvi road, a KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-36-F-574 driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner from opposite direction dashed against the motorcycle.

Due to the impact, the Phirojkhan vs Ravindra on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127402281/
2 claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: He took treatment as in patient and suffered loss of income due to disability.

Hence, the claimant has sought for compensation of Rs.45,50,000/-
with interest.

3. After hearing both the parties and considering the evidence forthcoming on record the Tribunal allowed the petition of the claimant in part granting compensation of Rs.7,92,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
The claimant contending that the compensation grant is meager has come up with present appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:15-DB HC-KAR 4.
The argument of the learned counsel for the claimant is that the Tribunal has committed error in fastening the liability on the claimant to the extent of 40% without any evidence.
Further, the compensation granted under the head of loss of earning during the laid up period is meager.
The Tribunal has not considered the future prospects of the claimant, even though the doctor has assessed the liability at 40% to the whole body.
He contends that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is meager as the claimant had suffered fracture of vital bones which was fixed using implants.
Besides, he contends that no compensation is paid towards future medical expenses even though the doctor had deposed that a sum of Rs.45,000/- would be needed for removal of implants.
Therefore, the learned counsel for the claimant has sought for enhancement of the compensation.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:15-DB HC-KAR 5.
Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has contended that the compensation granted by the Tribunal is just and reasonable and there is no reason for enhancement of the compensation.
Therefore, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 sought for dismissal of the appeal.
6. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for both the parties.
Perused the relevant materials on record.

7. As per the impugned judgment, the Tribunal determined total compensation of Rs.13,19,950/-
and came to the conclusion that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claimant to an extent of 40% in causing the accident.

It therefore proportionately awarded compensation of Rs.7,92,000/- with interest at 6% p.a.
8.

In the present appeal the respondent No.2 has not disputed the fact that the claimant sustained injuries in the accident involving the motorcycle of the claimant NC: 2026:KHC-K:15-DB HC-KAR and the above said KSRTC Bus.

The submission of the learned counsel for the respondents is that the Tribunal has rightly considered the notional income of the claimant and the disability as deposed by the doctor and awarded just and reasonable compensation under the head of loss of future earnings.

Phirojkhan vs Ravindra on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127402281/
3 9.

However, as submitted by the learned counsel for the claimant and also as forthcoming from the papers on record, it is clear that the claimant suffered grievous injuries such as:
i. Comminuted fracture neck of right femur, ii. Comminuted fracture shaft of right tibia with Type 111 B open wound femur, iii. Fracture of right Trocanter and iv.
Fracture neck of 4th and 5th meta carpel.
10. The vital parts of the right lower limb was severely affected resulting in temporary disablement.
Therefore, the compensation towards pain and suffering can be reasonably determined at Rs.25,000/- per fracture of vital bones.

Hence, the compensation of Rs.21,200/-
NC: 2026:KHC-K:15-DB HC-KAR awarded by the Tribunal under the head of pain and suffering deserves enhancement.
Therefore, the compensation amount under the head pain and suffering is enhanced to Rs.75,000/-.

11. Moreover, considering the nature of the injuries suffered and the period of treatment taken by the claimant, he must have suffered loss of income for a period of three months during the treatment.

Hence, the compensation under the head of loss of earning during the period of treatment is enhanced to Rs.45,000/- (Rs.15,000/- x 3).
12.

Further, as argued by the learned counsel for the claimant, even though the doctor has deposed in his evidence that the claimant would require expenses towards future medical treatment, such as surgery for removal of implants, the Tribunal has failed to grant any compensation under the head of future medical expenses.

Even though it is mentioned in the impugned judgment NC:
2026:KHC-K:15-DB HC-KAR that the compensation of Rs.1,54,350/- is awarded under the head medical expenses and future medical expenses, the said amount is the amount already spent by the claimant towards his treatment as per the medical bills at Ex.P.10.
Therefore, the above said amount does not include the expenses towards future medical expenses.

Hence, under the circumstances,
considering the medical evidence on record, an amount of Rs.45,000/- is awarded as compensation under the head of future medical expenses.

As argued by the learned counsel for the respondents,
the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads are just and reasonable.

13. The documentary evidence in the form of charge-sheet produced by the claimant at Ex.P.3 would show that after investigation the police filed the charge- sheet against the claimant and also against the respondent No.1, who were rider of the motorcycle and the driver of the KSRTC Bus respectively,
alleging that the accident took place due to rash and negligent riding of the NC: 2026:KHC-K:15-DB HC-KAR motorcycle and driving of the KSRTC bus by the claimant and the respondent No.1 respectively.

Therefore, there is no error committed by the Tribunal in coming to the conclusion that there was negligence on the part of the claimant to the extent of 40% and thereby determining the compensation at 60%.

14. In view of the discussion made above, we are of the considered view that the total compensation is enhanced as the following:

4  (in Rs.)
 1 Pain and suffering 75,000  2 Food and Nourishment, 20,000  conveyance and  attendant charges
3 Medical expenses 1,54,350
4 Loss of income during 45,000  the period of treatment  5 Loss of future earning 10,94,400  6 Loss of amenities 10,000
7 Expenses towards future 45,000  medical treatment

As stated earlier, there was negligence on the part of the claimant to an extent of 40% and therefore, 40% of the above determined compensation amount should be reduced towards contributory negligence on the part of claimant.
Hence, the claimant is entitled to 60% of the compensation re-determined by this Court, as above and therefore, he is entitled to compensation of Rs.8,66,250/- with interest at 6% per annum.
The compensation awarded is just and reasonable.

16. Since the liability of the respondent No.2 being owner and self-insurer, is undisputed, the respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

17. In the result, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part and therefore, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
- 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:15-DB HC-KAR ii.
The claimant/appellant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.8,66,250/- as against the compensation granted by the Tribunal at Rs.7,92,000/-.
iii. The respondent No.2 shall pay the compensation amount with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

5 iv.
The compensation amount with interest shall be deposited by the respondent No.2 before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

v. The enhanced compensation amount being meager, upon deposit of the amount,
the entire enhanced compensation amount shall be paid to the claimant.
vi. An award shall be drawn accordingly.
